headline: TypeSafe AI launches Jev model that outputs probabilities, not text
summary: A new AI model from an OpenAI co-founder eschews language for probabilities, promising lower costs, faster speeds, and no hallucinations for software automation.
details: A new transformer-based model named Jev has been released by TypeSafe AI, a startup founded by an OpenAI researcher who helped develop RLHF. Unlike traditional LLMs, Jev does not output text but rather probabilities, which the company calls "calibrated decisions."

This approach makes Jev significantly cheaper and faster to run. Because users define the expected outputs, the model cannot hallucinate, and its output tokens are free. Input tokens are metered by the billion, not the million, making it a potentially cost-effective solution for software automation.

Developers are showing strong interest in Jev. Early tests show it can be 5 to 18 times faster and more accurate than models like OpenAI's ChatGPT Luna 5.6 for tasks like command safety reviews. Another test against Gemini for business email classification found Jev to be 10 to 20 times cheaper.

Jev's output includes confidence scores, providing real probabilities that are ideal for automating workflows. It can also serve as a "System One" model, acting as a smart check on LLMs to prevent jailbreaks and monitor agent behavior, making agent-to-agent monitoring more feasible.

The model is named after William Stanley Jevons, referencing the Jevons paradox, which suggests that falling costs can lead to increased usage. TypeSafe AI believes Jev will enable widespread, emergent, and distributed intelligence in software, akin to the early internet rather than monolithic "mega apps."

TypeSafe AI trained Jev exclusively on synthetic data using a technique called "reinforcement learning from calibrated decisions." The company views its proprietary synthetic data generation as a key competitive advantage, even more significant than its previous work on RLHF.
